title: Region IV Conference Slideshow

card.teaser: A 22-slide conference presentation, built on a template I designed and that was voted in.

summary: A 22-slide conference slideshow for the 2026 NIRSA Region IV Conference, built on a template I designed and that was voted to be used.

hero.alt: The opening slide of the Region IV conference slideshow: Welcome, October 21 to 23, 2026, Corpus Christi, Texas.

text: As a design intern in the Recreational Sports marketing department at Texas A&M University–Corpus Christi, I designed the slideshow for the 2026 NIRSA Region IV Conference, held in Corpus Christi on October 21–23, 2026 and hosted by TAMUCC.
The slideshow runs through the opening session: a welcome, the Region IV network and its board, association highlights, the NIRSA Foundation, sponsors, the planning committee and the keynote speaker.

deliverables: A slideshow template for the conference
The previous slideshow's information, adapted into the new template
finalDesign: The 22 slides share one system. Section labels are set in spaced-out capitals, a footer repeats the conference location and dates, and numbered divider slides split the deck into sections, so both the presenter and the audience can tell where they are.

Most of the work was making dense information easy to read from the back of a room: board lists, award counts, event dates, roundtable schedules and strategic priorities each got their own layout inside the same template.
pull: I designed the template, and it was voted in.

rows.heading: A template, voted in
rows.body: The conference needed a slideshow, so I designed a new template in Canva. It was voted to be used for the Region IV conference: dark navy, Montserrat, and spaced-out capitals for section labels.
rows.alt: Four slides from the new template: the title slide, a numbered section divider and two content slides, in dark navy with spaced-out capital section labels.
rows.caption: The new template: title, section divider and content slides.

rows.heading: Moving the old slideshow into it
rows.body: Then I took the previous slideshow and adapted its information into the new template, rethinking each slide's layout instead of pasting the content in.
rows.alt: Three slides from the previous slideshow on the left, each beside the same information rebuilt in the new template on the right.
rows.caption: Before and after: the previous slideshow (left) and the new template (right).
